what_its_for: This medicine is a strong steroid (corticosteroid) that is applied to the skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching, and irritation caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema (atopic dermatitis), psoriasis, allergic reactions, rashes, and other inflammatory skin problems. The solution form is especially useful for hairy areas of the scalp or skin.
how_to_take: 1. Wash your hands before and after applying this medicine. 2. Gently clean and dry the affected skin area before use. 3. Apply a thin layer of the solution to the affected area and rub it in gently. 4. Do NOT bandage, wrap, or cover the treated area with plastic wrap or tight dressings unless your doctor tells you to — this can increase the amount of medicine absorbed into your body. 5. Avoid getting the solution in your eyes, mouth, nose, or vaginal area. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. 6. Do NOT use on broken, infected, or open skin unless your doctor has instructed you to do so. 7. Do NOT use more than prescribed — using too much or for too long can cause serious side effects.
dosing: Apply a thin film of the solution to the affected skin area 2 to 4 times daily, or as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not use this medicine for longer than prescribed — typically no more than 2 consecutive weeks without re-evaluation by your doctor. For scalp use, part the hair and apply drops directly to the scalp, then spread gently.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT apply a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep away from heat and open flames — this solution is FLAMMABLE, so keep it away from fire, sparks, and cigarettes. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze. Do not store in the bathroom medicine cabinet where it may be exposed to heat and moisture.
what_to_avoid: 1. Avoid using this medicine on your face, groin, or underarms unless specifically directed by your doctor, as skin in these areas is thinner and absorbs more medicine. 2. Avoid getting it in your eyes — it can cause eye damage including glaucoma or cataracts with prolonged use near the eyes. 3. Avoid applying to large areas of your body or using for longer than recommended. 4. Avoid using on children without strict medical supervision, as children absorb more through the skin. 5. Avoid tight bandages or plastic wraps over treated areas unless instructed. 6. Avoid using near open flames or while smoking — this solution is flammable. 7. Do not use other skin medicines on the same area unless your doctor approves.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical attention if you notice: 1. Skin infection signs such as increased redness, warmth, pus, or pain at the application site. 2. Skin thinning, stretch marks, or skin color changes. 3. Excessive hair growth (especially in children). 4. Acne-like bumps or pimples at the application site. 5. Your condition is not improving after 2 weeks of use or gets worse. 6. Signs of too much steroid being absorbed into the body: unusual weight gain especially around the face or belly, swelling, muscle weakness, easy bruising, extreme tiredness, increased thirst or urination, or vision changes. 7. In children: slow or stunted growth, unusual weight gain, or behavioral changes. 8. Any allergic reaction signs: severe rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement in redness, itching, and swelling within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement may take 1 to 2 weeks depending on your skin condition. If you do not see any improvement after 2 weeks, contact your doctor — do not continue using the medicine without guidance.
special_populations: CHILDREN: Use with extra caution in children. Children absorb more medicine through the skin than adults, which increases the risk of serious side effects such as slowed growth and hormonal problems (adrenal suppression). Use the smallest amount for the shortest time possible. Do not use on diapered or diaper area skin in infants. ELDERLY: Elderly patients may have thinner, more fragile skin and should use this medicine carefully to avoid skin breakdown or bruising. PREGNANT WOMEN: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Large amounts of topical steroids may harm an unborn baby. Do not use on large areas of skin or for long periods during pregnancy without medical advice. BREASTFEEDING: If you are breastfeeding, do not apply this medicine to the breast or nipple area, and ask your doctor if it is safe to use. LIVER DISEASE: Patients with liver problems should be monitored closely, as systemic absorption may be higher.
